title: 1956 Grand Canyon mid-air collision
summary: A TWA Constellation and United DC-7 collided over the Grand Canyon at 10:32 am in uncontrolled airspace. The two aircraft collided at an angle of about 25 degrees, and the DC-7's left wing clipped the Constellation's vertical stabilizer and fuselage, causing the tail assembly to break away. The Constellation entered a near-vertical terminal velocity dive and disintegrated on impact, while the DC-7 entered a rapidly descending left spiral and crashed into a cliff. All 128 people aboard both aircraft were killed.

title: KLM 607-E
summary: KLM Flight 607-E, a Lockheed Super Constellation named Hugo de Groot on the second leg of a transatlantic trip from Amsterdam to New York, crashed into the Atlantic Ocean after departing Shannon Airport, Ireland, on 14 August 1958. Radio contact was lost about 35 minutes after takeoff, and a rescue operation later found light debris and recovered the remains of 34 of the 99 people aboard roughly 180 km northwest of Shannon. summary: On December 16, 1960, United Air Lines Flight 826, a Douglas DC-8 heading for Idlewild Airport, collided in midair with Trans World Airlines Flight 266, a Lockheed L-1049 Super Constellation descending toward LaGuardia Airport. The Constellation crashed on Miller Field in Staten Island and the DC-8 in Park Slope, Brooklyn, killing all 128 aboard the two aircraft and six people on the ground. title: Sabena 548
summary: Sabena Flight 548, a Boeing 707 flying from New York to Brussels, made two aborted landing attempts at Brussels Airport on 15 February 1961 after a small aircraft had not yet cleared the runway. On a third circuit the aircraft's bank angle gradually increased until it reached a near-vertical bank at 1,500 ft; it then leveled its wings, pitched up abruptly, lost speed and spiraled nose-down into the ground near Berg, killing all 72 aboard and one person on the ground. Investigators could not conclusively determine the cause but believed the most likely explanation was a mechanical failure of the tail stabilizer-adjusting mechanism, possibly involving the wing spoilers.

title: Aviogenex 130
summary: Aviogenex Flight 130, an international charter from Gatwick to Rijeka, took off at 16:33 GMT and suffered structural failure during landing on 23 May 1971. title: British European Airways 548

title: Afriqiyah Airways 771

The crew made simultaneous sidestick inputs leading to a loss of control, and the aircraft crashed on terrain 1200 meters short of the runway, with only one child survivor.

title: Bhoja Air 213

title: Germanwings 9525
summary: Germanwings Flight 9525, an Airbus A320-211 with 150 people aboard, was deliberately crashed by first officer Andreas Lubitz into a mountain in the French Alps on 24 March 2015. After the captain left the cockpit for a scheduled break, Lubitz locked the cockpit door and set the aircraft to descend. The aircraft descended at an average rate of 3,400 feet per minute from 38,000 feet to impact terrain at 1,550 meters elevation. Investigators determined the crash was deliberately caused by Lubitz, who had been treated for suicidal tendencies.

title: Metrojet 9268
summary: Metrojet Flight 9268, an Airbus A321 charter flying tourists from Sharm El Sheikh to Saint Petersburg, exploded above the northern Sinai Peninsula on 31 October 2015 and crashed, killing all 224 people aboard. Radar and Flightradar24 data showed the aircraft climbing to 33,500 ft before suddenly descending and disintegrating in flight, scattering wreckage over 20 square kilometers with the tail separated from the forward fuselage; Russian investigators and the Islamic State's Sinai branch, which claimed responsibility, concluded a bomb had been placed aboard at Sharm El Sheikh.

events.text: At 06:13 EST on 31 October 2015 the Airbus A321 exploded above the northern Sinai Peninsula shortly after departing Sharm El Sheikh for Pulkovo Airport.

The flight failed to make contact with Cyprus air-traffic control 23 minutes after departure, and officials said it was at 31,000 ft when it disappeared from radar after a steep descent of 5,000 ft in one minute.

Flightradar24 data showed the aircraft climbing to 33,500 ft at 404 knots before suddenly descending to 28,375 ft at 62 knots about 50 km northeast of Nekhel, after which its position was no longer tracked.

Wreckage was scattered over 20 square kilometers, with the forward section about 5 km from the tail, indicating the aircraft had disintegrated in flight; aerial images showed the wings remained intact until impact.

The Islamic State's Sinai branch claimed responsibility for the crash, and Russian investigators concluded the most likely cause was an onboard explosive device that killed all 224 passengers and crew.
